intro: Fill this in at the site visit. Every number feeds the kitchen ballpark in JobTread, which prices Good, Better and Best at once. Write 0 when something does not apply; do not leave it blank.
screen: A structural wall is removed or opened
The sink, range or another fixture moves (drain, supply or gas line moves)
New foundation, footing or roof tie-in
HVAC extended or relocated beyond a register move
The cabinet layout changes or the room footprint changes
sections: Wall to wall, including any eat-in area being remodeled.
Walls opened and every cabinet out = 1. Cabinets and counters swapped with walls left intact = 0.
Walls framed, removed or relocated. Count each wall. Any structural wall means the design step.
1 for most kitchens. 2–3 when walls come out.
Linear feet of base cabinets, including the island and the width of any pantry or oven towers. Uppers are priced in; do not measure them.
Length of the island, already counted in the cabinet run. 0 if none.
Shape and run today, e.g. "L-shape, 22 ft, no island". For the estimator; not a formula input.
Count the sink, dishwasher, fridge water line and any pot filler that stay where they are.
Count each fixture whose drain, supply or gas line moves. An island sink counts.
Appliances DB buys for the customer. 0 if the customer buys their own.
Every appliance DB sets, including ones the customer buys.
Register moved or duct extended (toe-kick heaters count).
Circle one. Switching fuel adds a gas line or a 240 V circuit; count it above.
All new flooring, including any that runs into adjoining rooms.
Soft or damaged area you can see or feel today, often at the sink base or dishwasher.
New appliance circuits, GFCI runs and island outlets. A kitchen typically needs 2–4.
Circle one. A full panel may need an upgrade; flag it in notes.
Only when the job is past the standard service zone. Ask the CGM for the number.
tiers: Quartz slab to match the counters
photos: Cabinets open, including under the sink
